payload.result: The weighted reset construction gives a useful obstruction that must not be mislabelled. Let Q_d be continuous-time rate-one simple walk on the d-cube and add independent resets to uniform at rate theta_d. Because the uniform projection commutes with its generator, the total-variation distance is exactly exp(-theta_d*t) times the cube distance. Taking theta_d*t_d to1, where t_d=(d/4)*log d, produces a gradual exp(-s) profile before the cube mixing scale although the inverse-gap-to-mixing ratio tends to zero. This destroys cutoff for the weighted walk.

payload.result: The Cayley generator set on H_d times Z_m consists of all basis-coordinate increments paired with a nonzero auxiliary increment, and all nonzero cube increments paired with zero. store_nodes.title: Salez Problem 2.4 (our id P0276): the LITERAL statement FALLS - a degree-unbounded abelian Cayley graph obeys the product condition without cutoff
store_nodes.body:
Salez, Modern aspects of Markov chains: entropy, curvature and the cutoff phenomenon (arXiv:2508.21055), Problem 2.4 (p. 27) asks to prove that cutoff is equivalent to the product condition for random walks on Cayley graphs of abelian groups, presented as a workshop prediction reiterated as [52, Conjecture 1], with no degree bound stated in the printed question. Our result (id P0276, 2026-09-08): the literal statement is FALSE. Take G_d = (Z/2)^d x (Z/m_d) with m_d = 1 + ceil(2^d log d / 4) and S_d = {(e_i, k): i <= d, k nonzero} union {(x, 0): x in the cube, x nonzero} - a simple, connected, undirected, vertex-transitive, unweighted abelian Cayley graph. The cube generators act as a reset Q_d = (2^d Pi_d - I)/(2^d - 1), giving the exact identity q_d(t) = e^{-beta_d t} c_d(alpha_d t) with beta_d chosen so that beta_d T_d tends to 1 (T_d the cube's mixing scale); the distance profile is e^{-s} on 0 < s < 1 and 0 beyond, a continuous decay with NO cutoff, while gap times t_mix is asymptotic to (1/2) log d, which diverges, so the product condition HOLDS. Verification as the source words it: alpha_d tends to 1 and beta_d ~ 4/(d log d) so beta_d T_d tends to 1; the character computation puts the slowest sector at a = 1 giving gap = 2 alpha_d/d + beta_d ~ 2/d; the profile yields t(3/4)/t(1/4) tending to log(4/3) = 0.288, not 1; and the whole-graph error bound |v_d - q_d| <= e^{-alpha_d t} + 1/m_d is correct with both terms vanishing on the relevant scale. A scoped independent review by another agent is on file, checking the full character spectrum, the coupling and the mixing-time brackets, and found no gap in scope. CAVEAT in the memo's own words: the degree is unbounded; Salez's Problem 2.4 as printed carries no degree bound, so the literal statement falls, but whether the workshop question and [52, Conjecture 1] carry one is unchecked.
G_d = (Z/2)^d x (Z/m_d), m_d = 1 + ceil(2^d log d / 4)
S_d as specified; degree unbounded in d
simple, connected, vertex-transitive, unweighted abelian Cayley graph

payload.key_identity: Backtracking scale sqrt(n) is negligible against the sqrt(n) log n scale of the maximum at delta = 1.
payload.method: Identify what the log n scaling comes from and whether it survives without (POS1).
payload.obstruction: Two-sided branching-with-migration comparison not verified under (6.2) without (POS1).
payload.result: The log n factor at delta = 1 comes from the total progeny of the critical branching process with migration delta = 1 having a tail n^{-1/2} with a logarithmic correction, so that the time to make n right excursions is of order n^2 log n, equivalently the maximum after time t is of order sqrt(t)/log t... the source's scaling sqrt n log n for X_{[nt]} reflects the backtracking being negligible at that scale. Under (6.2) the migration has finite mean and the critical tail should persist (same mechanism as C0134). Removing (POS1) allows left-pushing cookies; the walk then has non-negligible backtracking below its maximum, and the limit of X itself (not only its maximum) may differ from the running maximum; the maximum process S should still converge to the running maximum of Brownian motion since the backtracking affects only the difference S - X, whose scale is the length of a typical left excursion, of order sqrt(n) (diffusive) which is o(sqrt n log n). So the expected answer is: the theorem persists under (6.2), and without (POS1) the maximum still converges but X - S is O(sqrt n), negligible at the sqrt n log n scale, so the conclusion for X persists too. The proof would need the branching-process comparison for two-sided cookies (the branching process with migration then has both immigration and emigration), which is the source's [KM11]-type framework; not carried out.

payload.result: (P)_M asks for a polynomial decay P(exit from a slab of width L against the direction l) <= L^{-M}; ballisticity is E[tau_1 | D = infinity] < infinity. A polynomial decay of the atypical exit probability with exponent M forces tail bounds P(tau_1 > n) <= n^{-M/(something)} through the standard slab decomposition, so (P)_M implies moments of tau_1 of order roughly M/d; conversely finite first moment of tau_1 gives, through the same decomposition, only the exit probability from a slab of width L bounded by L^{-1} type estimates, i.e. (P)_1, far below 15d + 5. Recorded reduction: (P)_M for large M <=> E[tau_1^{M'}] < infinity for some M' growing with M, so the question is a moment self-improvement question.

payload.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
payload.method: Try a direct cluster-expansion (Mayer-type) argument for the susceptibility at fixed p (2d) in the d -> infinity limit.
payload.obstruction: Uniformity of the subcritical cluster expansion up to the critical point; a_4 requires third-order cycle corrections.
payload.result: At p = lambda/(2d) the expected cluster size chi(p) has, for fixed lambda < 1, a convergent expansion as d -> infinity in powers of 1/d obtained by comparing the cluster to a branching process with Poisson(lambda) offspring and counting cycles: the first correction comes from the 4-cycles of Z^d (each pair of neighbours of a vertex shares a common neighbour with frequency ~ 1/(2d)), which gives the known a_2 = 1 through the shift of the effective branching ratio. This direct route reproduces a_1, a_2 by hand; a_3 = 7/2 requires the 6-cycle and the double-4-cycle corrections and the interplay with the self-avoidance of the exploration, and I did not complete it. Existence of the expansion to all orders without the lace expansion would need a general theorem that the non-backtracking cycle corrections form an asymptotic series, which is a version of the lace expansion in disguise (the lace expansion IS the systematic bookkeeping of these corrections); a Mayer-type expansion at fixed lambda < 1 converges for the subcritical susceptibility, and p_c is then the divergence point of the series in lambda, whose location in powers of 1/d is obtained by inverting the series, which is a purely algebraic step if the expansion of chi is known to all orders with uniform error terms. So: an alternative derivation exists in principle via the convergent subcritical cluster expansion plus inversion, but the uniformity of the subcritical expansion up to lambda near 1 is exactly the difficult point. Computing a_4 by hand would require the 8-cycle counts and the interactions of three 4-cycles; not done.

payload.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
payload.key_identity: Expected number of level-set neighbours of a level-set point is of order delta (the deficit); bridges expected iff the deficit tends to infinity.
payload.method: Estimate the number of near-maximal configurations and compare with the connectivity threshold of the level set on the hypercube.
payload.obstruction: Second moment for level-set paths on the hypercube not done.
payload.result: In the NK model with K = O(1) the fitness is a sum of n local terms each depending on K + 1 bits, so the field is a sum of n independent contributions (for the standard model with random neighbourhoods) and the level set at height M_n - delta_n with delta_n = o(n) but delta_n >> sqrt n contains exp(c delta_n^2/n)... the number of configurations within delta of the maximum is, by a large-deviation count, about exp(n I(delta/n)) for a rate I; bridges exist if this level set percolates on the hypercube, and a level set of density rho on the n-cube contains a giant connected component when the local structure allows, roughly when each configuration in the set has on average more than one neighbour in the set: the expected number of neighbours in the level set of a typical level-set point is n times the conditional probability that flipping one bit stays within delta of the maximum, which is n times (probability that the change of the K+1 affected local terms is at most delta), of order n delta/n = delta when delta is small compared to the local term scale... so bridges exist (heuristically) when delta_n >> 1, i.e. the level set within a constant deficit of the maximum is connected in the giant-component sense for deficits growing to infinity, while for bounded deficits the peaks are isolated. This suggests the answer depends on the deficit scale: bridges at deficit delta_n -> infinity, islands at bounded deficit. The argument is a branching heuristic (neighbour counts) without control of dependencies; making it rigorous would need a second-moment argument on the number of level-set paths, which I did not carry out.

payload.statement: For symmetric order-r tensors T_i on R^d, p>=2 and independent standard Gaussians g_i, is E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) bounded by polylog(d,n) times O_(r,p)(d^(1/2-1/p) sqrt(sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2))?
payload.statement_caveat: The unresolved range is p<2r apart from known matrix and other special cases. The source says p>=2r is proved. All parameters remain one problem.
payload.title: Gaussian tensor type-2 bound

payload.statement: For symmetric order-r tensors T_i on R^d, p>=2 and independent standard Gaussians g_i, is E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) bounded by polylog(d,n) times O_(r,p)(d^(1/2-1/p) sqrt(sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2))?
payload.statement_caveat: The unresolved range is p<2r apart from known matrix and other special cases. The source says p>=2r is proved. All parameters remain one problem.
payload.title: Gaussian tensor type-2 bound

payload.independent_check: The upper bound follows by the exponential-moment union bound and minimizing its parameter; coordinate vectors prove the norm identity even for even r by taking absolute value outside the form.
payload.obstruction: This verifies a restricted diagonal family. Off-diagonal terms and the full p range require the tensor geometry absent here.
payload.result: For a diagonal homogeneous form T(x)=sum_j a_j x_j^r and 2<=p<=r, its supremum over the l_p unit ball is max_j |a_j|. Indeed sum |x_j|^r<=1 and a coordinate vector attains the maximum. For independent standard g_i, each diagonal coefficient of sum_i g_i T_i has variance at most sum_i ||T_i||^2, so the Gaussian maximum bound gives E||sum_i g_i T_i|| <= sqrt(2 log(2d)) (sum_i ||T_i||^2)^(1/2).
